links.took: Grid-based turn-by-turn combined-arms tactics led by Commanding Officers with distinct unit buffs and signature powers.

src.t: Wikipedia: Advance Wars 2: Black Hole Rising

links.took: Scoring longer words and high-value letter tiles through vocabulary mastery across a shared tile grid.

links.took: PopCap's bright, low-friction casual cascade loop where clearing tiles drops fresh pieces into place with snappy audio feedback.

src.t: Wikipedia: Bookworm (video game); PopCap Games studio lineage

links.extra: PopCap's word-puzzle hit later spun off into Bookworm Adventures' turn-based RPG battles.

links.took: AKI Corporation's tap-versus-hold grapple system, momentum meters, and crisp counter-reversal wrestling engine.

src.t: Wikipedia: Def Jam Vendetta; AKI Corporation

links.extra: AKI adapted the grappling foundation it perfected across WCW/nWo Revenge and WWF No Mercy.

links.took: Underground hip-hop brawling powered by AKI's grapple reversals, Blazin' finishers, and Def Jam artist rosters.
links.added: Broadened pure pro-wrestling rings into five swappable martial-arts styles, environmental crowd-weapon hazards, and deep character customization.

src.t: Wikipedia: Def Jam: Fight for NY

links.took: Namco's horizontal scrolling rhythm-note track built around hitting distinct percussion zones in time with pop songs.

src.t: Wikipedia: Donkey Konga; developed by Namco's Taiko team

links.took: First-person Camera Obscura ghost exorcism rewarding players for snapping lethal Fatal Frame shots at the moment spirits lunge.

src.t: Wikipedia: Fatal Frame II: Crimson Butterfly

links.took: Iconic jobs, Moogles, elemental spells, and crystal mythology rooted in Square's flagship fantasy universe.
links.added: Rebuilt the series as a four-player GameCube caravan action RPG tethered to a protective Crystal Chalice and individual GBA link-cable radar screens.

links.took: Isometric grid-based tactical combat set in Ivalice with mix-and-match job classes and learned support abilities.

links.took: Seasonal crop tending, livestock care, village friendships, and marriage in a peaceful rural life simulation.

src.t: Wikipedia: Harvest Moon: A Wonderful Life

links.took: Masahiro Sakurai's copy-ability mechanics, bright Dream Land enemies, and multi-mode anthology structure.

src.t: Wikipedia: Kirby Air Ride; directed by Masahiro Sakurai

links.took: HAL Laboratory's snappy couch-multiplayer party energy and achievement-driven unlockable trophies.

src.t: Wikipedia: Kirby Air Ride; HAL Laboratory / Masahiro Sakurai

links.took: Rockstar North's RenderWare 3D engine, gritty urban wasteland aesthetic, and shared fictional universe referencing Carcer City.

links.took: Line-of-sight shadow hiding, sound-luring wall knocks, and radar-tracked enemy alertness phases.
links.added: Turned espionage evasion into visceral psychological horror where holding an attack behind hunters charges increasingly brutal improvised kills.

links.took: Persistent-server class specialization, guild raids, social town plazas, and long-horizon RPG level grinding.
links.added: Reinvented the MMORPG as a bright 2D side-scrolling platformer popularized by free-to-play microtransactions and expressive chibi avatar fashion.
links.extra: Wizet's Korean hit helped pioneer the global free-to-play cosmetic Cash Shop business model.

links.took: Blue-sky Ferrari road trips across branching scenic highways raced against checkpoint timers with a passenger beside you.

links.took: Sega AM2's tactile brake-tap powersliding physics that turn sweeping corners into rhythmic high-speed drifts.
links.added: Merged AM2's crisp drift-steering mastery with OutRun's sun-drenched coastal vistas and seamless gear-shift slides.

links.took: Tightly modeled real-world city circuits where players earn Kudos points for chaining clean drifts, overtakes, and stylish lines.

links.took: The twin-stick neon vector shooter Easter egg originally built by Stephen Cakebread to test Xbox controllers inside PGR2's garage.
links.added: Broke out as a standalone Xbox Live Arcade launch sensation with HD bloom visuals, score multipliers, and escalating geometric enemy waves.

links.took: Raven Software's fluid Quake III-engine lightsaber dueling, Force push/pull physics, and dismembering melee stances.

src.t: Wikipedia: Star Wars Jedi Knight: Jedi Academy

links.took: Pre-mission blueprint waypoint planning, one-shot lethality, and synchronized go-code room breaches.

src.t: Wikipedia: Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six 3: Raven Shield

links.took: High-speed PS2 arcade jet dogfighting over fictional Strangereal wars framed by earnest operatic storytelling.

src.t: Wikipedia: Ace Combat 5: The Unsung War

links.took: Persistent 3D online group combat structured around tank, healer, crowd-control, and damage archetypes.

links.took: Behind-the-quarterback broadcast NFL simulation balancing playbook strategy with direct arcade-fluid player control.

links.took: Reading opponent tells, slipping punches cleanly, and timing devastating counter-hooks in one-on-one boxing duels.

links.took: Console-first sci-fi first-person shooting designed around dual-stick aiming, two-weapon loadouts, and cinematic alien-frontline warfare.

links.took: Multi-move Copy Abilities, expressive sprite combat, and cooperative buddy exploration.
links.added: Turned Kirby's linear stages into a sprawling non-linear Mirror World where four color-coded Kirbys split up and summon each other by cell phone.

links.took: Interconnected labyrinthine world design built around map discovery, secret switches, and backtracking for hidden collectibles.
links.added: Blended Metroidvania room-to-room exploration with Kirby's carefree flying platforming and four-player link-cable co-op.

links.took: Acrobatic handstand jumps, color-coded switch puzzles, and carrying keys to locked exit doors across compact single-screen stages.

links.took: First-person lock-on exploration, visor scanning lore, and interconnected alien biome backtracking crafted by Retro Studios.

links.took: Compact single-screen puzzle-platforming rooms built around collecting scattered gold while outmaneuvering lethal automated traps.
links.added: Rebuilt room-clearing survival around fluid momentum-physics wall jumping, rocket-dodging parkour, and zero-delay Flash restarts.

links.took: Brutally unforgiving single-screen precision platforming driven by tight momentum control and instantaneous zero-downtime retries.
links.added: Paired Metanet's try-die-retry flow state with wall-sliding gore trails, simultaneous death replays, and unlockable Dark World gauntlets.

links.took: Third-person platforming fused with upgradable gadget arsenals, strafing gunplay, and arena gauntlets.

links.took: Team Silent's oppressive industrial nightmares, symbolic monsters, and Akira Yamaoka's unsettling soundscapes.
links.added: Anchored the horror in a chained first-person apartment hub that gradually turns hostile while adding real-time inventory limits and invincible haunting ghosts.

links.took: EA's 3D SAGE real-time strategy engine featuring cinematic special powers, leveling squads, and dramatic battlefield physics.
links.added: Replaced freeform base construction with fixed fortress building plots, multi-soldier battalions, and a living Middle-earth campaign map.

src.t: Wikipedia: The Lord of the Rings: The Battle for Middle-earth; EA Los Angeles SAGE engine

src.t: Wikipedia: Tom Clancy's Splinter Cell: Pandora Tomorrow

links.took: Dynamic shadow stealth refinement alongside the tense third-person Spies versus first-person Mercenaries online rivalry.
links.added: Expanded Sam Fisher's moveset with sound meters, close-quarters knife takedowns, co-op campaign missions, and open-ended sandbox infiltration maps.

src.t: Wikipedia: Tom Clancy's Splinter Cell: Chaos Theory

links.added: Adapted the action-RPG format to four-hero mutant squads with swappable teammates, destructible environments, and synced X-Treme super-combos.

links.took: Cinematic World War II Normandy storytelling inspired by Saving Private Ryan and Band of Brothers.
links.added: Replaced lone-wolf gallery shooting with authentic 'Find, Fix, Flank, Finish' squad suppression orders and an overhead situational-awareness view.

src.t: Wikipedia: Brothers in Arms: Road to Hill 30

src.t: Wikipedia: Destroy All Humans! (2005 video game)

links.took: Managing eccentric AI characters' moods, relationships, and vanity needs across customizable architectural lots.

links.took: Full-contact banger racing powered by soft-body chassis damage, flying debris, and reckless figure-eight demolition tracks.

links.took: Raven Software's four-player isometric superhero action-RPG engine with swappable teams and combo finishers.

links.took: Stacking falling colored blocks into a compact vertical grid to trigger matching-color chain clears.

links.took: Open-field tower defense where players sculpt their own winding mazes out of gun emplacements to redirect enemy waves.

links.took: Overhead urban crime mayhem where players tear through traffic-choked grids escaping escalating police barricades.
